prompt: Match each Team Topologies interaction mode to what it looks like.
hint: Lesson 10, the three ways teams work together.

pairs.right: two teams working closely for a while on something new
one team uses another's interface with little talking
one team helps another learn a capability

right_distractors: one team approves the other's designs

prompt: An architect writes a one-page note for the finance director about two structural options. What belongs in it? Choose all that apply.
hint: Lesson 10: options in the decider's units.

choices.text: Time and cost of each option, in reais
choices.why: Yes: the decider's units.

choices.text: The risk of each, as fines or delays
choices.why: Yes: risk said as consequences he protects against.

choices.text: The class diagram of the new service
choices.why: Only a technical reader would use it; he needs the consequences.

choices.text: What each option leaves behind for later
choices.why: Yes: what the option enables or costs next year is part of its price.

choices.text: A single recommendation, with no alternatives to distract him
choices.why: A single proposal invites yes or no; options invite a decision.

prompt: The integration manager at Carreto's bank partner can block a go-live but has no interest in how the service is designed. Where on the power and interest grid does she go?

choices.text: Manage closely
choices.why: Her interest in the design is low, so close management would cost her time for nothing.

choices.text: Keep satisfied
choices.why: Right: high power, low interest, like the accounting firm in the lesson.

choices.text: Keep informed
choices.why: That corner is for those with low power; she can block the go-live.

choices.text: Monitor
choices.why: Monitoring someone who can stop the launch is how a go-live gets blocked by surprise.

prompt: Two teams both change a shared notification module, and most of its incidents start where one team's change breaks the other's assumption. What does the lesson's approach suggest?

choices.text: A review step in which both teams approve each change to the module
choices.why: Two approvals keep the seam inside the module and add a queue.

choices.text: Rewrite it as a microservice owned jointly
choices.why: Joint ownership is what produced the incidents.

choices.text: One team owns it, and the other asks for changes through an interface it keeps
choices.why: Right: the managers arrange the ownership and the code follows.

choices.text: More tests on the module, written by the architect
choices.why: Tests help, but the cause is two owners each assuming different things.

prompt: A product manager asks for a feature that, unknown to her, breaks an assumption four teams rely on. What is the architect's first move, by the lesson?
hint: Lesson 10, the page Renata wrote for Helena.

choices.text: Refuse until the structure has been refactored
choices.why: That is the architect who says no, and product learns to route around him.

choices.text: Build it quietly and absorb the extra cost
choices.why: The structure pays silently, which is the other failure.

choices.text: Take it to the CTO to decide
choices.why: The priority is product's; the architect's job is the information.

choices.text: Write options with cost and risk; she chooses
choices.why: Right: options in her units, including what each leaves behind.

prompt: A company's architecture review board approves every design, and teams now bring it decisions they have already made. What change does the lesson point to?
hint: Lesson 10, a forum and not a board.

choices.text: Advise; the proposer decides
choices.why: Right: advice draws proposals early, while they can still change; the advice is recorded in the ADR.

choices.text: Meet more often so that the queue moves faster
choices.why: A faster queue is still a queue, and decisions still arrive made.

choices.text: Require slides so proposals are better prepared
choices.why: The forum's rule is no slides; the time is for questions.

choices.text: Make attendance mandatory for every tech lead
choices.why: Attendance is not the measure; which teams bring proposals is.
